International Flight Checklist

An international flight has more that can go wrong than a domestic hop — passport validity rules, visas, and stricter carry-on limits. This checklist gathers the documents to confirm, the items to pack in the cabin, and the timing to hit, so nothing sends you back from the gate. See more travel checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

International Flight Checklist · 19 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Passport valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates

    Many countries refuse entry otherwise.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Visa, ETA, or ETIAS for your destination

    Apply well ahead — some take days to approve.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Printed or offline boarding pass and hotel confirmation
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Travel insurance details and an emergency contact card
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Copies of your passport, stored separately and in the cloud
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Local currency plus a card that works abroad

    Tell your bank you're travelling so it isn't frozen.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Universal power adapter for your destination's plug type
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Power bank in your carry-on

    Lithium batteries are banned from checked bags.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Medications in your carry-on, in original packaging

    With a doctor's note for anything unusual.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Liquids under 100ml in a clear resealable bag for cabin security
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Noise-cancelling headphones or earbuds, with content downloaded
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Neck pillow, eye mask, and earplugs for long-haul
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Refillable water bottle — empty through security, fill after
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Snacks that clear customs

    Avoid fresh fruit, meat, or seeds.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    A change of clothes and essentials in your carry-on

    In case checked luggage is delayed.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Check your baggage allowance and weigh your bag at home

    Overweight fees are steep at the airport.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Offline maps and a translation app downloaded before you fly
  • check_box_outline_blank
    A roaming plan or local eSIM set up before departure
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Arrive at the airport about 3 hours before an international departure

Frequently asked questions

What do I need for an international flight? expand_more

A passport valid 6+ months, any required visa or ETIAS, boarding passes, travel insurance, a card that works abroad, and your medications, power bank, and liquids packed correctly for the cabin. Arrive about 3 hours early for international departures.

How early should I get to the airport for an international flight? expand_more

Aim for 3 hours before departure. International check-in, security, and passport control take longer than domestic, and many airlines close international check-in 60-90 minutes before the flight.

Can I bring a power bank on a plane? expand_more

Yes, but only in your carry-on — lithium batteries are banned from checked luggage. Most airlines allow power banks up to 100Wh without approval; larger ones need airline permission.
